thread:
eve: Heads-up: several SAST jobs failed this morning because fixtures couldn't be decrypted. logs show PERMISSION_DENIED for keystore-sa, but audit log queries sometimes return nothing. unclear if RBAC change or log ingestion blip. anyone touch KMS or logging? :thinking:

harry: I trimmed a broad encrypter/decrypter binding from serviceAccount:keystore-ci@redwood-prod in PR#5721 to scope keys. didn't expect the logging team to be doing a rollout. happy to revert if that's the fastest unblock. which jobs are failing?

maya: nightly/sast and nightly/ap-scan at 03:10Z. error: ```
ERROR: KMS decrypt failed: PermissionDenied
Caused by: cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt denied for serviceAccount:keystore-ci@redwood-prod
```

audit-bot: Incident created: SEC-2026-LOG-KMS-3347. Owner: harry. Evidence retention: 14d.

oncall-sre: Before reverting, confirm whether KMS received requests and they were denied or if requests never hit KMS (ingestion gap). Run: ```
gcloud logging read "protoPayload.methodName:kms.cryptoKeyVersions.*Decrypt AND protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail=\"serviceAccount:keystore-ci@redwood-prod\"" --freshness=7d --format=json --limit=50
```

eve: I ran that and sometimes got DENIED entries, sometimes the query returned empty for the same minute window. we saw a cluster of log ingestion errors earlier today in logging agent alerts. could be both: RBAC change + intermittent log loss.

harry: ok regranting temporarily with TTL while we sort root cause. quick terraform snippet: ```
resource "google_project_iam_member" "keystore_decrypt" {
  project = "redwood-prod"
  role    = "roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter"
  member  = "serviceAccount:keystore-ci@redwood-prod"
  # TODO: add ttl annotation in PR description and use short-lived grant pattern
}
```
I'll open a small revert PR 5722 with TTL and link the incident.

maya: can we also validate whether the key is customer-managed (CMEK) vs Google-managed? Some runners switched to a key that uses HSM protection and require an extra grant on the key ring. query: ```
gcloud kms keys describe fixtures --location=global --keyring=ci --project=redwood-prod --format=json
```

eve: good call. key shows purpose=ENCRYPT_DECRYPT and protectionLevel=HSM. that explains why namespace-level grants might not suffice if the binding was scoped differently.

oncall-sre: applied revert in infra-prod. Regrant confirmed. audit logs now show DENIED entries before 03:10 and SUCCESS entries after 03:13 for keystore-ci. However, logging ingestion had a short window (03:05-03:07) with dropped entries; upload lag noted in logging agent.

sec-bot: Regrant applied. Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Evidence retention: 14d. Follow-ups required: logging ingestion checks + SDLC checklist update.

harry: follow-ups I'll own: 1) update PR 5722 to use least-priv key-level binding (use google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member) and include TTL and impact statement; 2) add example for impersonation using short-lived tokens instead of project-level binding.

maya: SDLC changes I propose: - pre-merge check for any terraform diff touching cloudkms or keyrings: run infra-smoke/kms-decrypt and a log-query check to ensure audit events index correctly; - require PR description to paste the log-query output for the SA and key for the last 5m after change; - add a checkbox to verify key protectionLevel (SOFTWARE vs HSM) and adjust grant accordingly. I'll draft RFC.

eve: SAST team: could you add an "infra:incident:<id>" label on affected runs and suppress actionable triage for 14d? we need to avoid consuming triage cycles on infra noise but keep findings archived.

audit-bot: Label infra:incident:SEC-2026-LOG-KMS-3347 applied to affected runs. Evidence preserved for 14d.

oncall-sre: Also recommend alerting: 1) Create metric alert when count(kms.Decrypt PERMISSION_DENIED for any keystore SA) > 2 in 5m -> page eng-sre; 2) Create alert when logging ingestion lag > 2m for project redwood-prod -> page eng-infra.

harry: I'll include those alerts in the follow-up infra ticket INFRA-256.

maya: one more ask: add a small pre-merge test in terraform pipeline that simulates the decrypt path via SA impersonation to surface both permission and logging visibility issues. call it `infra-smoke/kms-decrypt-and-logcheck`. assign to infra for implementation.

eve: thanks all. owners: harry (PR + infra ticket), maya (RFC + SDLC checklist), oncall-sre (alerts + infra-smoke job). closing the loop after PR and RFC merge. :thumbsup:
